title: The communion of saints, again
hookLine: the saints you've met these five years are your company
tomorrow: why does every Hail Mary end at a deathbed?

cards: Scroll your contacts and you'll find a strange history: a coach from middle school, a cousin's ex, someone saved only as Dentist. The people who actually keep you company are fewer, and you'd know them by voice.
This path has been adding names you didn't have: Teresa of Ávila, who described prayer as friendship. Joseph, who said nothing and stayed. A whole crowd.
The letter to the Hebrews has a word for them.

teach.b: It says, in the Douay-Rheims, that we have "so great a cloud of witnesses over our head." Some readers hear a stadium: a crowd around the race, calling your name. The Church gives that crowd a sound.
At the Easter Vigil, at baptisms, at ordinations, a cantor sings the Litany of the Saints. A name, and the whole church answers: pray for us. Holy Mary, pray for us.
Saint Joseph, pray for us. Name after name, until the room fills up. That's the communion of saints, in your own voice.
It has a smell too: the candle lit in front of a statue, still burning after you've gone home.

teach.h: A CANDLE, A CARD, A MEDAL.
teach.b: And it has objects: the holy card in a wallet, the medal on a chain. Now the popular mix-up: people think Catholics worship saints. The Church says no.
Worship is for God alone. Asking a saint to pray for you is like asking a friend, except this friend is alive in God and has finished the race.
And notice how the Litany ends: with the people turning to God himself, asking him to hear them. The saints aren't statues, and they aren't the destination.

how: Catholics ask the saints to pray for them, light candles before their images, keep holy cards and medals, and sing the Litany of the Saints at the Easter Vigil, baptisms and ordinations.

games.q: what does “the communion of saints” mean?
o: the living and the dead, one family in prayer
a meal shared only by canonized holy people
a guild of saints who each rule part of heaven

games.q: how the crowd shows up — tap the pairs.
p: the answer in the Litany of the Saints
prayer that stays after you leave

s: worship is for God alone. asking a saint to pray for you is like asking a friend.
the Litany of the Saints is sung at baptisms and ordinations
a name, and everyone answers: pray for us.
only well-known, canonized saints belong to the communion of saints
it's the whole family in God: the living, the dead and the saints in heaven.

games.q: your friend's mom has surgery tomorrow, and your friend asks you to "get your saints on it." what fits the communion of saints?
o: ask a saint you know to pray for her mom, and pray yourself too.
explain that saints only pray for people who are Catholic.
light a candle, since the candle does the work, not the prayer.
games.why: the communion of saints is company: you ask them to pray with you, the way you'd ask a friend, and you pray too.

practice: Take a pen and write three saints' names down the side of a page, ones you've met on this path or grew up with. Say each one out loud, and answer it yourself, the way the Litany does: pray for us. Take your time with each name.

wordCard.voice: The communion of saints. The living, the dead and the saints in heaven, one family, praying for one another.

orig.note: Latin: pray for us. the answer sung to each name in the Litany of the Saints.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: my company, a crowd that already knows your name and keeps it. Talk tomorrow.
